sources.title: Roche: resources, disagreements and thesis choices in his2016 dialogue (2018issue/2023online)
sources.citation: Gil Bartholeyns interviews Daniel Roche, “Avis de recherche: Dialogue avec Daniel Roche (seconde partie),” Modes pratiques3(2018):157–169; interview1July2016, online26August2023. doi:10.54390/modespratiques.390.

verification.note: Fresh selected speaker-labelled HTML and official facsimile, selectedpp.160–164 and167–168, notes6–18/20/23/24;160/162/163 visually collated. Questions and DR answers distinguished. The 2018 issue,2016 conversation and2023 online date remain separate. Bracketed Foucault edition dates and an erroneous Labrousse birth year in the transcript are not adopted as new chronology/life facts. Complete books, lecture series and original recording unread.

hc176_daniel_roche_1.note: Dedicated Roche review: fresh selected first-part HTML/official facsimile, DR answers1/3/5/8/9/24/27/30/36, including printed172(Corbin),174(sugar/n7),175(Braudel),182(Brewer/Plumb/McKendrick). Specific resources and criticisms do not certify complete book reading. Modes pratiques2(2017),170–187; conversation1July2016 versus online28March2023. Earlier consumption qualifications preserved.

levi_biography_uses.note: Dedicated Roche review: freshly read official Persée per-page OCR1329–1332, especially1331, where Levi names Roche’s Ménétra as a contextual example, recognizes rich results, and warns that context can become too rigid to be changed by individuals. Olivier Christin’s translation credit retained. Original Ménétra introduction and complete book unread here; OCR accents/linebreaks not treated as exact quotation. This is a scoped fresh reading, not a new claim to collate all twelve pages.
